newsitem.title: UK: T&N warns some margins under pressure.
newsitem.headline: T&N warns some margins under pressure.

text.p: British components group T&N Plc said on Monday that operating margins in some product groups were being cut in the short term although other product groups continued to perform strongly and on target.

In comments on its earnings outlook that concluded that market uncertainties made it "particularly difficult to assess the final outcome for the year's results", a company statement said that demand for diesel products had been disappointing.
"Less buoyant conditions in the heavy duty and industrial markets, combined with de-stocking in the aftermarket..has so far kept factory output well below optimum levels," it added.
In general, T&N said, demand for original equipment for cars "had remained satifactory but patchy with requirements for diesel products disappointing".

"In the short term, these conditions are resulting in lower operating margins in those product groups which are most affected -- namely pistons, friction and gaskets -- although all other product groups continue to perform strongly, and well within the group's target range of return on sales."

"All businesses continue to reduce manning levels at a greater rate than in 1995, reinforcing the already sound base for ensuring that the group's overall margins are maintained in line with the target of averaging over 10 percent across normal business cycles," it concluded.

These comments were in line with comments in late August when company chairman Sir Colin Hope said the group took "a relaxed view" of its ability to bounce margins back over 10 percent again to keep its average intact.

Hope made that comment after the company's first half pretax profits slipped to 58 million stg and, at that time, the group also warned that full-year profits were likely to be below 1995's due to destocking and the effect of disposals.
